questions.q: In the Harrow Logistics scenario, which CI class should represent the order tracking application itself, separate from the servers it runs on?
options: cmdb_ci_server
cmdb_ci_appl
cmdb_ci_network_gear
cmdb_ci_database
questions.explain: The application itself is a cmdb_ci_appl record — distinct from the server hardware it happens to run on.

questions.q: Why do the web server and the application server each get their own separate cmdb_ci_server record, instead of one combined "server tier" record?
options: ServiceNow technically prevents more than one server per CI record
Each server has its own independently trackable state — one could go down for maintenance while the other stays up
There's no real reason; either approach works equally well
cmdb_ci_server only supports a single record per company
questions.explain: Separate CIs let each server's operational state be tracked and reported on independently, which a single combined record would lose.

questions.q: Why are the database server and the database instance modeled as two separate CIs rather than one?
options: Because cmdb_ci_database cannot reference cmdb_ci_server at all
Because the server (hardware/OS) and the database instance (data/schema) can each change independently of the other
Because ServiceNow requires a minimum of two records per application
Because this is simply a stylistic convention with no functional reason
questions.explain: The server can be patched and rebooted without the database instance changing, and the database can migrate to new hardware without its schema or instance name changing — separate records track each accurately.

questions.q: What class-specific fields would the Order Tracking Application's cmdb_ci_appl record carry, per this lab?
options: CPU count, RAM, and operating system
Port count and firmware version
Database type, schema, and instance name
Version, vendor, and business criticality
questions.explain: Version, vendor, and business_criticality are application-specific fields on cmdb_ci_appl — CPU/RAM belong to cmdb_ci_server, and db_type/schema belong to cmdb_ci_database.

questions.q: Why is this simple four-CI model already exposed to the data-quality risks described in Lesson 3?
options: Because four CI records is too many for any CMDB to track accurately
Because cmdb_ci_appl records cannot be created in a real instance
Because Discovery-scanned servers and manually entered application records could drift out of sync at different rates, with no named owner to catch it
Because this model has no data-quality risk at all
questions.explain: Mixed data sources (Discovery vs. manual entry) updating at different rates, combined with no named owner, is exactly the governance gap Lesson 3 described.
